title: How many students were absent in Class 2?
description: A bar graph shows the students absent in each of eight classes, with one unit of length for one student. Reading the top of one bar against the numbers on the left line gives the count, and Keeko's doubt, that the class number is the answer, is checked against the graph.
teaching_notes: One idea: the height of a bar is read against the numbers on the side line, and the label under the bar only names the class. Watch for students who give the class number instead of the number of students.

source: Answer the following questions using the bar graph: In Class 2, ___ students were absent that day.
video_script.why: The child learns to read one bar by going up from its label and across to the number scale.
video_script.substitution: Find the bar for Class 2, go to its top, and read the number on the left line at that height.
video_script.anchor: the bar graph of students absent in each class, with one unit of length for one student
video_script.wrong_answer: the answer is two, because it is Class two
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko reads the class label as the number of students. The label only names the class, and the count is read from the line on the left.
video_script.payoff_line: Five students were absent in Class two

final_answer.spoken: five students were absent in Class two

names.{{NAME_5}}: collects the absent-students data and makes the pictograph and bar graph

maths_rules: the bar for Class 2 reaches the line marked 5, so 5 students were absent
video_script.design: One idea: read a bar by going up from its label and across to the number line. The graph stays on the board all video and a pointer travels up the bar of Class 2.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a bar graph.
<bookmark mark='graph'/>{{NAME_5}} counted the students absent in each of eight classes and drew a bar for each class.
<bookmark mark='scale'/>One unit of length on the graph stands for one student.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many students were absent in Class two? How can the graph tell us?

beats.on_screen: the bar graph stays on the board and Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a small bar graph with one bar for Class 1 reaching the line marked 3; a pointer goes up the bar and across to the number 3 on the left line

marks.pic: a pictograph row of 3 smileys changes into one bar of height 3
marks.bar: the length of the bar is shown against the numbers on the left line
marks.three: the pointer goes up the bar and across to the number 3

narration: <bookmark mark='pic'/>In a pictograph we counted the symbols. In a bar graph, one bar does that job.
<bookmark mark='bar'/>The length of the bar tells us the number. The numbers stand in a line on the left.
<bookmark mark='three'/>A bar that reaches the line marked three shows three students.

beats.on_screen: Given: the bar graph of students absent in each class; 1 unit length = 1 student

marks.given: the words the bar graph of students absent in each class are written
marks.unit: the words 1 unit length = 1 student are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the graph shows the students absent in each class.
<bookmark mark='unit'/>One unit of length stands for one student.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number of students absent in Class 2

marks.find: the words the students absent in Class 2 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the number of students absent in Class two.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: find Class 2 on the line at the bottom; the bar above it is lit

marks.class: the label Class 2 on the bottom line is circled
marks.bar: the bar above the label lights up

narration: <bookmark mark='class'/>Step one, find Class two on the line at the bottom, because each bar stands above its class.
<bookmark mark='bar'/>The bar right above that label is the one we need.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: a pointer goes up to the top of the bar of Class 2 and then across to the numbers on the left line

marks.top: a pointer goes up the bar to its top
marks.across: a dotted line runs from the top of the bar across to the left line

narration: <bookmark mark='top'/>Step two, go up to the top of that bar, because the top shows how tall it is.
<bookmark mark='across'/>From there, look straight across to the numbers on the left line.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: the dotted line meets the left line at the mark 5

marks.meet: the dotted line meets the left line at the mark 5 and the mark is circled

narration: <bookmark mark='meet'/>Step three, read the number where the line meets the left line. It meets the mark five.
<bookmark mark='unit'/>Five unit lengths, and each unit stands for one student.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 5 students were absent in Class 2
narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Five students were absent in Class two.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is two, because it is Class two.
<bookmark mark='label'/>But the label under the bar only names the class.
<bookmark mark='line'/>The number of students is always read from the line on the left.
